CSCO.rationale: Cisco's fundamental trajectory is genuinely — Q3 FY2026 delivered record revenue of $15.84B (+12% YoY), 35% order growth, and AI orders raised to $9B target. However, the stock is extremely overvalued relative to its own history and the durability of this earnings acceleration. PE has expanded to 42.5x from a typical 25-30x range — a +51% multiple expansion that far exceeds the incremental margin and earnings improvements. The earnings yield of 2.4% sits well below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.57%, implying a negative equity risk premium of ~217bps. Operating cash flow declined 43.3% QoQ and 18.7% YoY, flagging a potential disconnect between accrual earnings and cash generation. Core networking excluding AI grew only ~4%, and the security segment remains flat-to-declining. The stock has surged +49.2% in one quarter, front-running what may take multiple quarters of sustained execution to justify. Morningstar's own fair value estimate is $90 — 24% below the current $118.20 price. A reversion to the historical median PE of ~28x would imply ~34% downside. The stock is priced for flawless execution with no margin of safety, and near-term downside catalysts (any deceleration in AI orders, OCF quality concerns, rate sensitivity) are material.
